name: Primary Cutaneous Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma
aliases: Primary Cutaneous CD30+ Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of large anaplastic CD30+ lymphoid cells with hallmark morphology in skin biopsy
Solitary or localized nodules or tumors on the skin without extracutaneous involvement at diagnosis
Strong CD30 expression in >75% of tumor cells with ALK negativity
No evidence of systemic lymphoma by imaging and bone marrow biopsy
T-cell receptor gene rearrangement demonstrating clonality

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of CD30+ anaplastic large cells in skin biopsy with typical clinical presentation and exclusion of systemic lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: ALK negativity distinguishes primary cutaneous ALCL from systemic ALCL

pathognomonic.symptomName: Solitary or localized ulcerated cutaneous nodules or tumors
searchTerms: single or few ulcerated skin nodules or tumors

pathognomonic.symptomName: Strong CD30+ expression on large anaplastic lymphoid cells in skin lesions
searchTerms: strong CD30 marker on large abnormal skin lymphoid cells
skin lesions with CD30+ immune cells
presence of CD30+ anaplastic lymphoid cells in skin

common.symptomName: Erythematous plaques or papules adjacent to nodules
searchTerms: red plaques or bumps near skin nodules
inflamed skin areas adjacent to tumors
erythematous skin lesions next to nodules
swollen lymph nodes nearby without fever
regional lymph node enlargement without systemic illness

common.symptomName: Spontaneous partial regression of skin lesions
searchTerms: skin lesions partially heal on their own
partial regression of skin spots without treatment

occasional.symptomName: Pain or tenderness at lesion site
Secondary bacterial infection of ulcerated lesions
Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever
small bumps surrounding main skin tumor

rare.symptomName: Extracutaneous dissemination (e.g., lymph nodes, bone marrow)
searchTerms: disease spread to lymph nodes or bone marrow
spread of disease to internal organs

rare.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
searchTerms: general body symptoms like fever and sweating
skin ulcers with tissue death and bleeding
ulceration with dead tissue and bleeding

laboratory: Histopathology showing large anaplastic lymphoid cells with hallmark morphology
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD30 in >75% of tumor cells
imaging: PET-CT or CT scan showing absence of systemic lymphadenopathy or organ involvement
other: Exclusion of systemic lymphoma by bone marrow biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: ALK positivity in majority of cases
Histology shows CD30+ atypical cells but less dense infiltrate

redFlags: Development of systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Evidence of extracutaneous dissemination on imaging or biopsy
references: Willemze R, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005.
Bekkenk MW, et al. Primary and secondary cutaneous CD30(+) lymphoproliferative disorders: a report from the Dutch Cutaneous Lymphoma Group. Blood. 2000.
Swerdlow SH, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC. 2017.
